result.summary: Adds UNIX domain socket support for the HTTP RPC server and bitcoin-cli via the -rpcbind and -rpcconnect options using unix:<path> syntax. It introduces UnixSocketAddr and a SocketAddr variant in netbase to decouple generic socket endpoints from P2P networking classes like CService, and refactors Proxy and HTTPServer to use them. When binding exclusively to UNIX domain sockets, -rpcallowip is no longer required and default TCP localhost listeners are omitted.
result.problem: Local RPC communication currently requires TCP loopback connections, requiring IP-level configuration like -rpcallowip instead of standard operating system filesystem permissions. Additionally, previous UNIX socket support in PR #27375 was isolated to the Proxy class, leaving technical debt where socket abstractions were tangled with P2P-specific networking types.
evidence: Closes issue #5029, a request for UNIX domain socket RPC support dating back to 2014.
Author notes the refactor pays off technical debt from PR #27375 by creating generic UnixSocketAddr and SocketAddr abstractions in netbase.
result.scope_notes: Touches netbase, HTTPServer, init, and bitcoin-cli, and updates the Python test framework with an optional --httpunix flag to run functional tests entirely over UNIX domain sockets.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased over recent changes including PR #36303, updating the interface_http.py flood test to identify connections via connection IDs rather than ephemeral ports.
result.card: Adds UNIX domain socket support to the HTTP RPC server and bitcoin-cli using the unix:<path> option syntax for -rpcbind and -rpcconnect. This allows local clients to use standard filesystem permissions instead of -rpcallowip, avoiding TCP loopback overhead entirely. The change also resolves long-standing technical debt from PR #27375 by introducing UnixSocketAddr and SocketAddr abstractions in netbase to decouple generic socket types from P2P classes. This closes issue #5029, an open feature request from 2014.

risk.why: A flaw in the new socket bind or access check logic could prevent bitcoind from accepting RPC commands or expose the RPC interface to unauthorized local processes.
